problem_text: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

ranking.title: Detection-branch veto: MVFA's image-label-trained detection maps filter pseudo-masks for the segmentation branch

Novelty.review: Using a weakly supervised branch to filter pseudo-labels is known (co-training, anomaly-guided weakly supervised OCT segmentation); using MVFA's own image-label-trained detection branch as the second view is a new, method-specific combination.

Feasibility.review: Needs only a det-only pre-training stage and a target filter; same cost as MVFA training on one GPU.

Clarity.review: Targets, agreement quantiles, ignore rule and stages are specified; how the detection map is read per level could be stated more precisely.

Impact.review: Directly answers whether image-level labels can replace masks for MVFA's segmentation branch, with the three image-only datasets usable as sources.

Validity.review: Sound: the detection branch is trained with reliable labels on all six datasets; its maps may be diffuse, which the ignore rule partly handles.

ranking.title: Detection-gated mean teacher: online pseudo-mask refinement accepted only where MVFA's detection branch agrees

Novelty.review: Combines a mean teacher with detection-branch gating; both ingredients exist in weakly supervised segmentation, the gating by MVFA's sibling branch is new.

Feasibility.review: One training run, but the teacher schedule and gate thresholds need joint tuning on source validation.

Clarity.review: Schedules, gating rule and losses are specified; the interaction of epochs and ramp is left to tuning.

Impact.review: Same practical question as the veto idea, with potentially cleaner targets.

Validity.review: Gating limits teacher drift; validity rests on the detection branch being better than the teacher where they disagree.

ranking.title: Occlusion attribution of MVFA's detection branch as pseudo-masks for its segmentation branch

Novelty.review: Counterfactual attribution for weakly supervised medical segmentation exists (COIN uses counterfactual inpainting); replacing patches by nearest normal-bank features of MVFA's own detection branch is a new, cheap variant.

Feasibility.review: 289 adapter-only forward passes per abnormal image with cached CLIP features: affordable but slower than other options.

Clarity.review: Attribution definition, threshold and training stages are clear.

Impact.review: Turns image labels into causal localisation evidence for MVFA.

Validity.review: Occlusion with nearest normal features is a principled counterfactual; diffuse detection maps could weaken attributions on OCT and chest X-ray.

ranking.title: Cross-level persistence pseudo-masks: anomalies that persist across MVFA's four feature levels

Novelty.review: Multi-layer anomaly evidence is common in anomaly detection; requiring persistence across exactly MVFA's four adapted levels as a pseudo-mask filter was not found in prior work.

Feasibility.review: Training-free, four nearest-neighbour searches per image.

Clarity.review: Fully specified rule with clear ablations (persistence 2, 3, 4).

Impact.review: A useful filter, but its benefit is limited to pseudo-mask precision.

Validity.review: The assumption that lesions are anomalous at all levels is argued by analogy; subtle texture-only lesions may be lost.

ranking.title: Mean-teacher online refinement of pseudo-masks during MVFA training

Novelty.review: Mean-teacher pseudo-label refinement is a standard semi- and weakly supervised technique; applied to MVFA without method-specific change.

Feasibility.review: Single run, extra EMA model; schedule tuning needed.

Clarity.review: Schedule, blending and ignore band specified.

Impact.review: Halves the cost of self-training, a practical but incremental gain.

Validity.review: Anchoring to initial masks and image labels limits drift.

ranking.title: Dawid-Skene fusion of MVFA-internal pseudo-label sources with per-dataset reliabilities

Novelty.review: Dawid-Skene and dependent weak-source aggregation exist; applying them to three MVFA-internal sources with normal images as known negatives is a new combination.

Feasibility.review: EM on patch labels is cheap; requires a det-only stage.

Impact.review: Gives per-dataset reliabilities that are informative beyond the masks themselves.

Validity.review: Conditional independence between sources sharing one CLIP backbone is violated, so posteriors may be overconfident.

ranking.title: Shift-ensemble pseudo-masks: sub-patch grid jitter doubles the effective resolution of MVFA's pseudo-masks

Novelty.review: Averaging ViT outputs over patch-grid phase shifts is described in recent work (phase marginalisation for patch-grid instability) and tiled ensembles.

Feasibility.review: Four feature extractions per image for mask generation only.

Clarity.review: Exact shifts, realignment and thresholds given.

Impact.review: Improves resolution of targets, most relevant for small brain lesions.

Validity.review: Directly addresses the verified 14-pixel grid limit.

Feasibility.review: Two trainings plus attribution make it the most expensive option.

Validity.review: Avoids self-confirmation by using a different branch for regeneration.

ranking.title: Two-round self-training: regenerating pseudo-masks from MVFA's own adapted features

Novelty.review: Two-round self-training with regenerated pseudo-labels is a standard technique (e.g. self-training for zero-label segmentation).

Feasibility.review: Doubles training cost; still feasible on one GPU.

Impact.review: Tests whether MVFA's adaptation improves localisation features, a useful diagnostic.

Validity.review: Risk of confirmation bias is acknowledged but only partly controlled by label restriction.

ranking.title: Size-constrained training of MVFA's segmentation branch from image-level labels

Novelty.review: Size-constraint losses for weakly supervised segmentation are established (Kervadec et al.); the application to MVFA is direct.

Clarity.review: Bounds, loss terms and sensitivity test specified.

Impact.review: Answers what image labels alone can teach the segmentation branch.

Validity.review: Robust to bound errors by design; bounds derive from noisy pseudo-masks.

ranking.title: Counterfactual normal-twin differencing: pseudo-masks from each abnormal image's most similar normal image

Novelty.review: Comparing registered query and normal images is the core of registration-based few-shot anomaly detection (RegAD) and counterfactual approaches.

Feasibility.review: Retrieval and ECC alignment are cheap; alignment may fail on OCT/CT.

Impact.review: Mainly benefits registered anatomy such as brain MRI.

Validity.review: Affine alignment is unreliable outside brain slices, limiting validity across BMAD.
